title: Adaptive heatmap-driven KV reseeder with probe-and-fill allocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe sustained micro-fragmentation in the KV cache on long-running hosts that gradually increases tail latency during high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads. Existing heuristics rely on coarse occupancy thresholds and full-slot rebuilds that are expensive and cause throughput degradation when triggered.

Goal: Implement a low-cost, incremental allocation strategy that prefers filling small micro-holes without global rewrite windows and that is aware of batching access patterns. The approach should reduce the need for heavy compaction, lower variance in request latency under sustained load, and be deployable behind a feature flag.

Summary of proposed solution:
- Maintain a lightweight per-GPU micro-heatmap that records short-term occupancy and access-density by small region buckets (micro-buckets sized to typical KV footprint quantiles).
- Use a probe-and-fill reseeder that opportunistically places new KV entries into detected micro-holes (gullies) using a sequence of increasing probe radii, avoiding disruptive global reassignments.
- Integrate batching affinity hints: the scheduler annotates request groups with predicted slot-size and locality info so the reseeder favours contiguous placements for hot batched prefixes to minimize cross-slot scattering.
- Implement background opportunistic reseeding during low-GPU-usage windows and coordinated slow-path reseed for regions exceeding a fragmentation threshold, with backoff to prevent noisy repair storms.
- Export heatmap and reseed telemetry to Grafana for visibility and to drive automated tuning (probe window, bucket size, low-util windows).

Why different from prior work: This ticket focuses on a "probe-and-fill" incremental placement strategy driven by a short-term heatmap and batching affinity signals rather than one-off compaction sweeps or size-tiered slab moves. It is designed to be lighter-weight and safer in multi-tenant Dedicated/Private contexts where heavy background rewriting is undesirable.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-heatmap implemented on the runtime with <2% additional GPU memory overhead measured on a 48GB instance
Probe-and-fill reseeder reduces mean KV hole count by >=40% in 24h sustained mixed-size continuous-batching workload (internal benchmark)
Tail percentiles (p95/p99) for generation latency improved or unchanged under identical throughput for benchmarked workloads
Feature flag gates end-to-end flow and can be disabled without restart
Telemetry dashboards (heatmap, reseed events, probe failures) exist in Grafana and are linked in the ticket
Automated safety limits: reseed rate per minute and per-GPU throttles implemented and validated
implementation_notes: Heatmap representation: circular buffer of fixed windows (e.g., 1s buckets over last 2 minutes) aggregated into micro-buckets of 64/128/256 token-sized regions depending on model profile
Probe strategy: randomized low-biased probe sequence (local-first) followed by exponential radius probes to avoid pathological clustering
Batch affinity: extend existing request metadata to include 'placement_hint' (size-class + locality-score) consumed by runtime placer
Reseeding schedule: background loop that runs when GPU util < 25% or during controlled maintenance windows; also a slow-path triggered when per-bucket fragmentation > threshold for > 5 minutes
Safety: per-GPU reseed token-bucket limiter, max writes per-second guard, and opt-out for Dedicated pools with strict write amplification SLAs
Migration plan: roll out to runtime-qa -> beta customers -> all-hosts behind feature-flag; telemetry gated at each step
Benchmark harness: extend 'kv-frag-bench' with mixed-size continuous-batching trace (trace from customer-X production sim) to measure hole-count, p95/p99 latency, and reseed overhead
updates: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial proposal written; shared design doc (links below) with infra and runtime leads for feedback.
2026-02-16 - Marco Nguyen: Prototype heatmap sketch implemented in runtime dev branch (PR pending); early memory overhead measured at ~1.4% on dev instance.

2026-02-20 - Runtime team review: agreed to use 3 micro-bucket sizes (small/med/large) and to piggyback placement_hint in the request context. Decided to avoid cross-tenant reseed during business hours.
2026-02-25 - Marco Nguyen: Probe-and-fill algorithm implemented behind feature flag; integrated basic telemetry for reseed events and probe latencies. Running canary on 5 hosts.
2026-02-28 - Observability: Grafana panels added (kv_heatmap_overview, reseed_events, probe_success_rate). Initial data shows hotspots resolving after reseed events in canary hosts.

2026-03-01 - Performance: micro-benchmarks indicate 35% reduction in hole count after 12h; tuning of probe radius suggested (reduce max radius by 25% to avoid write amplification). Next: expand canary and run 24h mixed workload test.
